related_questions.question: How to fix an irregular heartbeat?

text_blocks.snippet: An irregular heartbeat, or arrhythmia, can be addressed through a variety of methods, ranging from lifestyle changes to medical interventions. Treatment options depend on the type and severity of the arrhythmia, and the patient's overall health. Common approaches include medications, procedures like cardioversion or ablation, and lifestyle adjustments.
snippet_highlighted_words: medications, procedures like cardioversion or ablation, and lifestyle adjustments

list.title: Medications:
list.snippet: Doctors may prescribe medications to control heart rate and rhythm, prevent blood clots, and reduce the risk of stroke. These can include beta blockers, calcium channel blockers, and antiarrhythmic drugs.
Cardioversion: A controlled electrical shock or medication can be used to restore a normal heart rhythm.
Ablation: This procedure uses heat or cold to destroy the area of heart tissue causing the abnormal rhythm.
Implantable devices: Pacemakers and implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) can regulate heart rate and rhythm or deliver shocks to correct dangerous arrhythmias.
Diet: A heart-healthy diet low in salt and saturated fats, rich in fruits, vegetables, and whole grains, can improve overall heart health.
Exercise: Regular, moderate-intensity exercise, like cardio, can strengthen the heart and improve its function.
Weight Management: Maintaining a healthy weight reduces strain on the heart.
Stress Management: Techniques like meditation or yoga can help manage stress, a potential trigger for arrhythmias.
Substance Avoidance: Limiting or avoiding alcohol, caffeine, nicotine, and illegal drugs can reduce the risk of triggering arrhythmias.
Sleep: Prioritizing good sleep habits can also benefit heart health.
If you experience new or worsening symptoms of an arrhythmia, such as chest pain, shortness of breath, or dizziness, seek immediate medical attention.
Regular checkups with a doctor are important for managing and preventing heart rhythm problems.

text_blocks.snippet: Important Note: This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Consult with a doctor or other qualified healthcare provider for any questions you may have regarding your health or treatment options for an irregular heartbeat.
